# Behavioral Specification: CSRNG Main Command State Machine

## 1. Overview

This module is the main command-sequencing state machine for a CSRNG application command. Its role is to receive one command request at a time, determine which command is being requested, perform any required preparation, issue the corresponding command request, and then wait until the command has completed before returning to the idle state.

The module does not perform cryptographic operations. It only controls the sequencing of command acceptance, command decoding, entropy-gated preparation, command request generation, additional-data clearing, and command-completion waiting.

## 2. Reset and Enable Behavior

- After reset, the module must be in the idle state and all outputs must be deasserted.
- When the module is disabled, it must remain idle and must not accept any new command request.
- While disabled, the module must not assert any command request, entropy request, header-capture, clear, or error indication.
- If the module is disabled while processing a command, it must return to the idle state on the next cycle and deassert all active outputs. It must not wait for the command to complete.
- The only exception is the error state: once the error state is entered, the module must remain there and continue asserting the error indication until reset, even if the module is disabled.

## 3. Command Acceptance

The module must accept a command only when all of the following conditions are true:

- The module is enabled.
- The module is idle.
- A command request is available.
- The downstream command-processing path is ready to accept the command.

When these conditions are met, the module must assert a command-accept indication for one cycle and then move to the command-parsing state.

The module must not accept more than one command at a time. While it is processing a command, it must not issue a new command-accept indication until that command has completed and the module has returned to idle.

## 4. Command Parsing

In the parsing state, the module must wait until the command-processing path is ready and the current header word is marked as the end of the command header. When both conditions are true, the module must decode the command value.

The five defined command types are:

- Instantiate
- Reseed
- Generate
- Update
- Uninstantiate

When a valid command type is decoded, the module must:

1. Assert a header-capture indication for one cycle.
2. Move to the preparation state corresponding to the decoded command.

No command request output shall be asserted during parsing.

If the end-of-header marker has not been seen, the module must remain in the parsing state and continue waiting. No action shall be taken for reserved or undefined command encodings.

## 5. Preparation and Entropy Gating

The preparation state for each command determines whether external entropy is required before the command request can be issued.

### 5.1 Instantiate and Reseed

For an instantiate or reseed command, the behavior depends on the first command flag.

If the first command flag is clear:

- The module must assert an entropy request.
- It must remain in the preparation state until entropy is available.
- When entropy is available, it must move to the corresponding request state.

If the first command flag is set:

- The module must not request entropy.
- It must proceed to the corresponding request state as soon as the preparation state has been entered.

### 5.2 Generate, Update, and Uninstantiate

For generate, update, and uninstantiate commands, no entropy request is required. The module must proceed from the preparation state directly to the corresponding request state.

## 6. Command Request Generation

When the module enters a request state, it must assert the appropriate command request output for exactly one cycle:

- Instantiate command: assert the instantiate request.
- Reseed command: assert the reseed request.
- Generate command: assert the generate request.
- Update command: assert the update request.
- Uninstantiate command: assert the uninstantiate request.

After issuing the command request, the module must move to the additional-data clearing state.

## 7. Additional-Data Clearing

In the additional-data clearing state, the module must assert the clear-additional-data indication for one cycle. This ensures that any buffered additional data from the current command is cleared.

After this clearing cycle, the module must move to the command-completion waiting state.

## 8. Command Completion and Return to Idle

In the command-completion waiting state, the module must wait for the command-complete indication.

- If the indicator is not asserted, the module must remain in this state.
- When the command-complete indication is asserted and the module is enabled, the module must return to the idle state.
- After returning to idle, the module may accept the next command.

No command request outputs, entropy request, header-capture, or clear-additional-data outputs shall be asserted while waiting for command completion.

## 9. Error Behavior

The module is required to detect an illegal state-machine encoding. If such an illegal state occurs:

- The module must enter the error state.
- It must assert the error indication continuously.
- It must not issue any command request, entropy request, header-capture, or clear-additional-data output while in the error state.
- It must remain in the error state until reset.

## 10. Summary of Functional Requirements

- The module must not accept commands while disabled or while processing another command.
- The module must only generate command requests for the five defined command types.
- Entropy must be requested only for instantiate and reseed commands, and only when the deterministic-seed flag is clear.
- The module must issue exactly one command request per processed command.
- After a command request, the module must clear the additional-data path and wait for command completion.
- Completion must be indicated before the module returns to idle.
- Any illegal state encoding must cause a persistent error indication until reset.
